name: Alyssum Carpet of snow
sowingInstructions:
Sow Outdoor In a prepared seed bed in flowering.Sow thinly in rows 15cm apart. Cover with 0.5cm fine soil When large enough thin to 15cm apart
Firm gently and keep moist Seedlings appear 14-28 days
careInstructions:
Keep moist and weed free.
Trim plants as flowers fade for a second flush of blooms.

name: Aubergine Alexandra
description:
Solanum melongena L.
Semi-early eggplant variety. It has oblong, pyriform fruits, dark purple to glossy black, weighing between 200-300 g. Recommended for cultivation in the open field. Vegetation period: 80-90 days, medium early.

name: Aubergine Black Beauty
description: A heavy cropper, noted for its reliability in the greenhouse and outside in full sun. Sturdy plants produce a heavy crop of pear-shaped fruits with a high sheen to their skins. The large purple-black fruits are ready to crop in as little as 78 days from sowing, providing a constant crop right through to autumn. Germination: 10-14 days (65-70°F) Plant height: 60cm (24in)
plantingOutInstruction: When the seedlings are large enough to handle, carefully transplant them into 7.5cm (3in) pots and grow on at a slightly reduced temperature. When all risk of frost is passed and the soil is warm, harden off and plant in their final positions. For indoor cultivation, pot on into larger containers or plant 2 per growbag. Outdoors, plant in rich fertile soil at a distance of 90cm (3ft) apart, in rows spaced 90-120cm (3-4ft) apart. Planting through black polythene mulch will help to warm the soil, control weeds and save moisture.
sowingInstructions: Soak seeds in warm water for 24 hours before sowing will assist germination. Sow seeds on the surface of a free-draining, moist seed compost and cover with 6mm (1/4in) layer of vermiculite or compost. Place in a propagator or seal the container inside a polythene bag at constant temperature of 18-21°C (65-70°F) until after germination
careInstructions: Support plants with canes and remove sideshoots for the best yields. Never allow soils/compost to dry out and feed regularly once the first truss has set.

name: Beetroot burpees golden
description: A mild tasty variety which remains tender. The orange roots turn golden-yellow when cooked and have a wonderful flavour and texture.
sowingInstructions:
In a prepared seed bed
Sow thinly in rows 30cm apart
Cover with 2.5cm of fine soil
Firm gently and keep moist
Seedlings appear 7-21 days
For continuous crops sow every 2-3
weeks
careInstructions:
When large enough thin to 10cm apart
Keep moist and weed free

name: Beetroot Detroit
description:
Reliable performer
Deep, dark red colour Outstanding beet for over 100 years
sowingInstructions: Sow seeds thinly, about 2cm (1in) apart in pre watered shallow rows, and cover with a little soil. Allow about 30cm (12in) between rows.
careInstructions:
Growing Tips
Supplied as multigerm seeds, several plants in one seed. Use thinnings as baby leaf salad. When harvesting beet, twist the tops off the roots rather than cutting them. This prevents bleeding.

name: Begonia Cascading mix
description: Suitable for flower beds, borders, containers on the patio and balcony. Also suitable as a houseplant.
sowingInstructions: Plant outdoors, hollow part uppermost, when all danger of frost has passed. Keep the soil moist and remove faded flowers. At the end of the season, lift the tubers, cut the stems off just above the tubers and store in a dry soil at 4-10 degrees.

name: Bell Pepper Artim
sowingInstructions:
Plante de vigoare medie. Fructele sunt conice, rotunjite la vårf, de culoare galben ceruit, cu coacere in rosu intens
la maturitatea fiziologicä. Potential de productie ridicat.

name: Bell Pepper Daciana F1
description:
Blocky bell pepper hybrid with indeterminate growth.
The fruits are large, yellowish-green in color and have weight
average of 140-180 g. Recommended for field or protected space.

name: Bell Pepper Sweet Californian wonder
description:
Capsicum annuum
A thick pendula sweet pepper. Great in cooking or raw in
salads. Continuous flowering over a long period.
plantingOutInstruction: Once all chance of frost has passed the plants can be transplanted into growing beds or patio tubs outside, harden off first.
sowingInstructions:
Indoor Planting:
Sow seeds 5mm deep in pots or trays of moist compost, store in a warm place at an approx. temperature of 18-21°c (65-70°f).
careInstructions: These plants do best in very mild conditions, therefore, it would be better to keep them in a greenhouse or indoors.

name: Bell Pepper Vlad gogosar
description:
Perioada de vegetatie: 140-145 zile. Fructe mari,
cu suprafata netedå 5i 4-5 loji seminale. Pulpa
este groasä. Culoare verde tnchis la inceput,
rosie la maturitate. Soi productiv.

name: Broad Bean Aquadulce Claudia
sowingInstructions:
Sow outdoors, where they are to crop,
5 cm deep, directly into finely-prepared,
well-cultivated, fertile soil, which has already
been watered. To make the best use of space,
sow seeds 23 cm apart, in a wide row
in a zigzag pattern, leaving a space
of 60 cm between each row. Sow a few
extra seeds at the end of the rows to fill
in any gaps produced by seeds that don't germinate-
Seedlings will usually appear after 10 - 18 days.

name: Broccoli Autumn Calabrese
description:
(Brassica oleracea var. cymosa)
A quick growing variety, producing mild flavoured large green heads. Ideal for freezing.
sowingInstructions: Sow seeds 1.5cm deep in trays of moist compost, be careful not to over-water. Store in glass house. Plant out in desired location in June - July.

name: Broccoli CALABRESE Ironman F1 Hybrid
description:
Sow regularly through Feb-June for full-season use Consistent head quality and uniformity
A quick-cropper ready to harvest in as little as 75 days after transplanting. Calabrese Ironman F1 shows good tolerance to hollow stem and resistance to bolting. Suitable for closer spacing for baby head production, or simply because growing space is tight.
plantingOutInstruction: Choose a sheltered position in firm, rich fertile, well drained soil in full sun. Prepare the soil in early spring by adding plenty of well rotted farmyard manure to the soil to improve its structure and fertility. Take care when transplanting Calabrese as it resents root disturbance. Plant Calabrese at a distance of 45cm x 45cm for full sized hearts, 30cm x 30cm for 'baby' hearts at closer spacing, and cover with a protective netting or fleece to prevent attack from birds and insects. Water the plants thoroughly after planting.
sowingInstructions: Sow seeds in a well-prepared seed bed from February to June at a depth of 13mm (1/2in) and spaced 30cm (12in) apart. Transplant to their final positions around 5 weeks later when the seedlings have four or five leaves.

name: Broccoli clared f1
description: An extremely vigorous and heavy cropping variety with great tasting large and tender shoots. Plants go on to produce many side shoots, giving a long harvest period.
plantingOutInstruction: When large enough to handle transplant 5cm apart in trays of compost Stand outside for a few days late May (avoid frosts). Transplant in June to final position with 60cm between plants and rows
sowingInstructions: Sow thinly, cover with 1.5cm of compost. Firm gently and keep moist Keep at approx. 13°C. Seedlings appear 7-21 days
careInstructions: When harvesting Cut shoots when 10-15cm long Pick young shoots regularly to encourage further cropping

name: Broccoli Early purple sprouting
description:
Brassica oleraces
An easy to grow variety, producing lots of purple heads with an excellent flavour during late winter/early spring. The heads will turn green when cooked. Broccoli is high in Vitamin A and C and a good source of iron.
plantingOutInstruction: hen the plants are 4-6 weeks old plant out in desired location. Harden off first. Harvest by snapping off the flowering shoots before the flowers open.
sowingInstructions:
Indoor Planting:
Sow seeds 1.5cm deep in trays of moist compost, be careful not to over-water.
careInstructions: Keep the soil moist, and be careful not to over-water.

name: Brussels Sprout Brodie F1
description:
The mildest and sweetest Christmas sprout
• So tasty, with no bitterness, that even the kids will love them!
• Add bacon & chopped chestnuts for extra crunch and flavour
After years of trialling and tasting, has Thompson & Morgan found a replacement for our long-standing customer favourite 'Trafalgar? Very round, well spaced, 38mm buttons of mild flavour with a much reduced
mustard oil aftertaste. Later forming buttons into the New Year can be slightly larger (45mm), but maintain their perfect quality.
plantingOutInstruction:
GROWING INSTRUCTIONS: Transplant when large enough to handle into well prepared, firm soil allowing 75cm (30in) between plants each way. Plant firmly to
reduce risk of poor quality buttons and plants leaning over. Water until established. Earth up the soil around plants as necessary to increase stability. Remove yellowing leaves to improve air circulation and reduce disease risks. Pick lowest sprouts first and
work up the stem.
sowingInstructions: SOWING INSTRUCTIONS: Sow in individual pots or a seed compost and cover with 6mm (1/4in) of compost or vermiculite, at a minimum of 15C, until germination which usually takes around 7 days. Alternatively, can be sown thinly in a prepared seedbed 13mm deep, allowing 30cm between rows.

name: Cabbage Cabbice F1
description:
A super sweet variety producing crunchy, round
heads approx. 2kg in size. The unique flavour lends
itself well to salads, as well as more traditional dishes.
plantingOutInstruction:
Transplant to final position
45cm a art. Firm in well
sowingInstructions:
In trays of seed compost
Sow thinly, cover with a fine layer of
compost. Firm gently and keep moist
Cover with glass, polythene or propagator
lid. Keep at approx. 130C
Seedlings appear 7-21 days
Remove cover when seedlings appear
When large enough transplant 5cm apart
in trays. Stand outside for a few days to
acclimatise.
careInstructions:
Avoid diseases such as club root by
rotating Brassica crops yearly

name: Cabbage Offenham (flower of spring)
description:
Brassica oleracea Capitata
A very popular and reliable variety with good flavour. The dark green heads are suitable for use as tasty 'greens' or as a 'hearted' spring cabbage.
sowingInstructions:
In a prepared seed bed. How Sow thinly in rows 25cm apart
Cover lightly with 1.5cm of fine soil. When 5-6 leaves have formed, transplant to final position 25cm apart for 'greens', or 45cm apart for hearted cabbages Firm in well and keep moist
commonProblems: Avoid diseases such as club root by rotating crops yearly

name: Cabbage Primo
description:
Brassica oleracea Capitata
Compact plants that produce very firm and dense medium sized ball-headed cabbages through the summer. Has an excellent, mild flavour.
plantingOutInstruction: Transplant to final position with 45cm between plants and rows.
sowingInstructions:
In trays of moist compost
Sow thinly, cover with a fine layer of compost and firm gently. Keep at approx.
13°C and keep moist
Seedlings appear 7-21 days When large enough to handle transplant
5cm apart in trays of compost Gradually acclimatise to outside conditions

name: Cabbage ruby ball F1
description:
Dense, solid, crunchy hearts
Sweet-flavoured, cooked or raw
Superb for long storage over winter
An early maturing, vigorous and uniform Red Cabbage with deep red, solid and compact heads. Their remarkable sweet flavour and high quality make them ideal for cooking as well as pickling.
sowingInstructions:
Sow thinly in a well-prepared seedbed, 1 cm (1/2in)
deep, successionally, and plant out when large enough to handle allowing 38cm apart each way.
Alternatively seeds can be sown into containers under glass and transplanted into pots or trays when large enough to handle. These young plants can be
grown on in a cold frame until large enough for transplanting into their final positions.

name: Calendula Art shades mix
description:
An easy to grow annual for bedding and borders. The large, frilled blooms come in unusual shades ranging through apricot, orange, primrose and cream. Long-flowering for four months of summer colour, also makes a good cut flower. The petals can be used as a substitute for saffron, and in a variety of dishes where they make a bright and zesty addition. Excellent for bedding and borders
Large frilly flowers in golden colours from summer to autumn Will grow in any well-drained soil in full sun
sowingInstructions:
Sow outdoors where they are to flower. Prepare the ground well and rake to a fine tilth before sowing. Sow 12mm (½/in) deep, in rows 30cm (12in) apart. When large enough to handle, thin out seedlings to
23-30cm (9-12in) apart.
FOR SPRING/SUMMER FLOWERING POT PLANTS: Sow in a cool greenhouse or conservatory in late summer/early autumn. Grow on through winter in cool, frost-free conditions in full light and water sparingly.

name: Calendula Indian prince
description: Bold and eye-catching deep orange blooms with a rich mahogany red on the reverse of the petals. Long stems make it a perfect cut flower for indoor displays.
sowingInstructions: Outdoor sowing Sow thinly in a prepared seed bed in flowering position, in rows 25cm (10in) apart. Cover lightly with 0.5cm (quarter inch) of fine soil, firm gently and keep moist. Seedlings usually appear in 7-21 days. Make 2-3 sowings for successive flowering.
careInstructions: When large enough thin to 23cm (9in) apart. Keep moist and weed free. Late sowings flower the following year.

name: Carrot Amsterdam Forcing
description:
Daucus carota
An excellent easy to grow variety producing small, tasty roots. Very quick to mature and ideal for forcing.
sowingInstructions:
Outdoor Planting:
Sow seeds thinly 1.5cm deep direct in growing beds in rows 12" (30cm) apart. Keep the soil moist, and be careful not to over-water. When large enough to handle thin to 4" (10cm) apart.
For early crops, sow in a cold frame or under cloches during February and March.
careInstructions: The carrots will be more tender and tasty if harvested before maturity.

name: Carrot Early Nantes
description:
Daucus carota
As its name suggests this is an early variety producing blunt ended carrots of excellent flavour. Ideal for freezing.
sowingInstructions:
Outdoor Planting:
Sow seeds thinly 1.5cm deep direct in growing bed in rows 12" (30cm) apart. Keep the soil moist, and be careful not to over-water. When large enough to handle thin to 4" (10cm) apart.
Ideal for successional sowing.
careInstructions:
The carrots will be more tender and tasty if harvested before maturity.
Keep well watered in dry conditions.

name: Carrot Flakker
description: Late, vegetation period 200-220 days. The dry matter content is high, so it is excellent for storage. The root is 23 cm long, 5 cm wide with a pointed end.

name: Cauliflower
plantingOutInstruction: Stand outside for a few days early April (avoid frosts)
sowingInstructions:
For indoor sowing
When: January to March
Where: In trays of seed compost
How: Sow thinly, cover with a fine layer of compost. Firm gently and keep moist
Keep at approx. 13°C
Seedlings appear 14-28 days
careInstructions:
Care
Transplant to further trays if necessary
Stand outside for a few days early April (avoid frosts). Transplant to final position with 60cm between plants and rows
Firm in well and keep moist
When approx. 10cm tall transplant to final position with 60cm between plants and rows. Firm in well, keep moist and weed free
Harvest June to October
Tip: Protect early and late (overwinter) sowings with cloches

name: Cauliflower Depurple F1
description:
Depurple retains its colour if steamed or lightly boiled,
and the tasty florets are also rich in antioxidants.
plantingOutInstruction:
Planting Out - Plant into the required harvest position
45cm apart with 45cm between each
row when plants have 3-4 true leaves.
October sowings can be overwintered
in a cold frame and planted out in
March for the earliest harvests.
Transplanting - When seedlings have produced
4 leaves, transplant them to their cropping position leaving 45cm between plants in rows 45cm apart.
Firm in and keep well watered in dry spells.
sowingInstructions:
Sow Indoors-  Sow thinly, lcm deep in clean trays or
modules of firm, pre-watered compost.
Keep soil moist at all times.
Sow Outdoors - Sow thinly, lcm deep in a seed bed
or clean module trays of firm, pre-
watered compost. Keep soil moist at all
times. Thin to 10cm.
careInstructions:
Advice - Use netting to prevent damage from
Cabbage White Butterfly.

name: Cauliflower romanesco precoce
description: Sometimes referred to as broccoli this unusual vegetable has a distinctive sweet nutty taste and is widely favoured by restaurant chefs.
plantingOutInstruction: When approx 10 cm transplant to final position with 60cm between plants and rows. firm in well, keep moist and weed free
sowingInstructions:
In trays of seed compost. Sow thinly, cover with a fine layer of
compost. Firm gently and keep moist. Keep at approx 13C. Seedlings appear 14-28 days
careInstructions:
Protect curds from direct sunlight by
folding in the leaves

name: Celery Green Sleeves
description:
Almost stringless pale green flesh, great crunch and flavour Easy to grow, stands well and is slow to bolt
•High in fibre
plantingOutInstruction:
Transplant seedlings 5cm (2") apart to other trays when large enough to handle. (Always handle by a leaf, never by the stem.) Grow on in cooler, but not cold conditions.
Gradually accustom young plants to outside conditions (avoid frosts), before planting out 25cm (10") apart. Allow 30cm (1) between rows. Water well
sowingInstructions:
Sow indoors 0.5cm (½/4") deep, in a tray of compost.
Water well and place in a cold frame, greenhouse or on a cool windowsill. A temperature of 15-20°C (60-68°F) is ideal. Keep moist. Seedlings usually appear in 14-21 days.

name: Celery Tango f1
description:
Excellent for use in soups and salads
Early maturing to extend the harvest season
Low maintenance and easy-to-grow.
A self-blanching variety with beautiful apple-green, smooth stems with good flavour and texture for that all important celery crunch. Good bolting resistance and stands well during hot weather for reliable crops.
plantingOutInstruction:
Transplant when seedlings are large enough
to handle into modules or small pots of compost and maintain a minimum temperature of 15C. Harden off and plant outside in well-prepared soil once all frost risk has passed allowing 30cm (15in) between each plant.
Plant in block formation to assist with self-blanching. It is essential to keep well watered for succulently flavoured, string-free stems.
sowingInstructions: SOWING INSTRUCTIONS: sow thinly in seed trays or pots of good seed compost at 15-20C. Sow on the surface of the firmed compost and cover with a very fine layer of vermiculite.

name: Chamomile
description:
CHAMAEMELUM NOBILE
Charming daisy like flowers over deliciously sweet smelling, fine foliage. Use flowers to make chamomile tea. Hardy perennial. Height up to 30cm.
sowingInstructions:
FOR OUTDOOR SOWING
Where In a prepared seed bed in a
When April to June sunny growing position How Sow thinly in rows 30cm apart, do not cover seeds.
careInstructions:
Keep moist Care When large enough to handle, thin
to 30cm apart Tip Cut back after flowering to promote new leaf growth To use as a tea, add 1 tsp of chopped fresh herbs per mug of boiled water, leave to brew for 3-5 minutes and strain

name: Chard Bright lights
description:
Beta vulgaris
Up to 7 different colour stems which can be picked as baby leaf or full size. Steam leaves and stems separately and get two dishes for the price of one!
sowingInstructions:
Sow Outdoor In a prepared seed bed
with 2.5cm fine soil. Firm gently and keep moist. Seedlings appear 14-28 days. For continuous crops sow every 2-3 weeks
careInstructions:
When large enough thin to 15cm apart Keep well watered to prevent bolting and weed free. Pick individual stems as required. For baby leaves, thin to only 7.5cm apart and cut leaves when 5-10cm tall. They will regrow for several cuts July to November. Through winter if given cloche protection. Provide a liquid feed every two weeks to
increase yields

name: Chilli pepper dwarf purple (romania)
description: Chilli pepper dwarf turns red when ripen.

name: Chilli Pepper Jalapeno M
description:
Mild and tasty flavour
Attractive bright green and red fruits
Widely known as the 'pizza pepper', this jalapeho is the most widely used
and popular selection. Dark green, turning bright red fruits are 8-10cm
long, thick-walled and slightly tapered with blunt ends. For use in a variety of
dishes - not just sliced on your favourite pizza!
plantingOutInstruction:
FOR INDOOR CROPS: Plant 2 plants per growbag or individually into 20cm 
pots or 2 litre pot. For optimum results grow under glass.
FOR OUTDOOR CROPS: Gradually acclimatise plants to outdoor conditions for 10-15 days before planting one plant per 20cm or 2 litre pot, or a larger
container on the patio. Plant in final position from early June when there is no
further risk of frost and protect from biting winds. Feed plants weekly with a high potash tomato fertiliser once first fruits have set.
sowingInstructions: Sow seed on the surface of a good, free-draining damp seed compost and cover with a fine sprinkling of compost or vermiculite. Place in a propagator or seal container in a polythene bag and keep at 25C until after germination which takes up to 14 days. Transplant seedlings when large enough to handle into 7.5cm (pots. Reduce temperature and maintain at 15C

name: Chinese carnations
description: A very variable species that is native to a vast area, from Europe into Asia. A short-lived herbaceous perennial, but plants bred from this species are often grown as annuals or biennials. Single flowers with fringed edges are typically pink, but can be white or red, often with a dark purple central ring or eye, held above green leaves
sowingInstructions: For best results, seeds are sown directly into the ground where required in the spring. Alternatively, sow in late winter/early spring in gentle warmth, 15-20 degrees C. Prick out into small 3 inch or 7 cm. pots and plant in final position when the plants are established.
pruningInstructions: Deadhead regularly to prolong flowering. Lightly trim after flowering or in spring
careInstructions: Grow in a well-drained soil in a sunny position

name: Chinese Lantern
description: Physalis alkekengi
plantingOutInstruction:
Indoor Planting:
Sow the seeds 0.5cm deep in trays of moist compost, be careful not to over-water. Store in a warm, light place not in direct sunlight at an approx. temperature of 15-20°c (60-70°f).
Growing On:
Spacing 24" / 60cm
When the seedlings are strong enough to handle they can be transplanted into bigger pots or trays.
sowingInstructions:
Sow Indoors
A wonderful decorative plant, with beautiful bright orange lantern shaped flowers. Popular in winter flower arrangements. Hardy Perennial.
Sow Outdoors May - July
Outdoor Planting:
Sow seeds 0.5cm deep in flowering location, thin to above spacings.
Any well drained soil will do. Thrives in a sunny position.
careInstructions: Do not overcrowd the plants and keep in a warm, light position. Once all chance of frost has passed the plants can be transplanted direct into your desired location. Harden off first.

name: Chives
description:
Allium schoenoprasum
Can be grown in pots or even in the flower border. The mild onion flavour is ideal in salads or added to dairy sauces and all types of egg dishes.
plantingOutInstruction: Thin plants to further pots or trays if necessary. To grow outdoors, stand outside for a few days late in May (avoid frosts) plant out 20cm apart. To grow indoors, transplant to 15cm pots of compost, place in a light airy location.
sowingInstructions: In pots or trays of moist compost. Sow thinly, cover lightly with compost and firm gently. Cover wirh clear glass, polythene or propagator lid. Keep at 15-20 degrees and keep moist. Seedlings appear 14-28 days. Remove cover when seedlings appear.

name: Chives Garlic
description:
Excellent in salads, stews, fish, egg or meat dishes
Easy for all to grow
A must have for the herb garden. 
Garlic chives differ from ordinary chives in having flat leaves and have a delicate mild garlic flavour. They can be used in the same way as chives and are excellent in salads, stews, fish, egg or meat dishes.
plantingOutInstruction: GROWING: Transplant seedlings into 7.5cm pots. Grow on in cooler conditions for a few days before planting out after all risk of frost has passed, 30cm apart.
sowingInstructions:
WHERE TO SOW: Start off in a seed tray or pots indoors or direct outdoors once soil has
warmed.
PREPARATION: Indoors - fill a seed tray or pots with good, free-draining, seed compost.
SOWING: Sow seed on the surface of the compost and cover with a sprinkling of compost
or vermiculite. Place in a propagator or seal container inside a polythene bag and keep
at 20-25C until after germination which takes up to 21 days. Do not exclude light, as this helps germination. Can also be sown outdoors once the ground has warmed, 13mm deep, in rows 20cm (8in) apart

name: Courgette Blanco de virginia 3
description: Early bush-type variety with erect and compact habit. Elongated fruits up to 35 cm long in light green color. Very productive. Pale flesh has excellent flavor.
plantingOutInstruction: Plant out from March - June at a distance of 40-50 cm
sowingInstructions: Sow indoors Feb- Mar and directly outdoors May -june. Keep a temperature of 12-14C

name: Courgette defender hybrid
description:
Twice the cropping power of other courgettes! The open habit of the plants also makes it easier to see the many solid, mid-green, heavy fruits. Crops well through the season without trouble, thanks to Cucumber Mosaic Virus resistance.
SERVING SUGGESTION: Use fresh courgette flowers stuffed with ricotta cheese or
rice and vegetables.
plantingOutInstruction: GROWING INSTRUCTIONS: Gradually acclimatise to outdoor conditions for 10-15 days before planting out after all risk of frost, 60cm (24in) apart. Can also be sown direct outdoors once the soil has warmed. Sow 2 seeds every 60cm (24in) and thin out to the best seedling.
sowingInstructions: SOWING INSTRUCTIONS: Sow seed, 1cm (1/2in) deep in 7.5cm (3in) pots of free draining compost. Place in a propagator or seal container inside a polythene bag and place at 20-25°C (68-77°F) until after germination which takes 7-10 days. Do not exclude light, as this helps germination.

name: Courgettes Cerna (romania)
description: Fast-growing, the fruits are cylindrical, finely ribbed, weigh 2-4 kg, the skin is light yellow. The plant is thermophilic and sensitive to low temperatures. Successful cultivation requires regular irrigation and nutrient supply.
plantingOutInstruction: After 45 days plant out 50cm apart
sowingInstructions:
Indoor sowing: Feb- March or Jul- Aug
Outdoor sowing Apr-May

name: Courgettes Goldena
description: Cucurbita pepo cylindrica
plantingOutInstruction:
Gradually accustom plants to outside conditions (avoid
frosts), before planting out 60 cm apart, into fertile,
well-drained soil, growing bags or 40 cm diameter
pots, during May-June when frosts are over.
sowingInstructions:
Sow indoors 1.5 cm deep, on edge, in 7.5 cm pots of seed compost. Water well and place in a warm position. A temperature of 15-20°C Seedling - Courgette is ideal.
Seedlings will usually appear after 7-14 days
careInstructions: Keep the soil constantly moist by watering around the plants, not over them. Top Tip! Plant a small, empty growing pot alongside the plants. Water into the pot and it will help ensure that water goes right down to the roots and doesn't sit around the neck of the plant which could lead to rotting.

name: Cucumber Cornichon de Paris
description:
Vegetation period: 65 days. Small fruits of
dimensions 9/2 cm. Green fruits, with grooves and thorns
blacks. flowering is mixed. Good productivity.

name: Cucumber Crisan (for pickles)
description:
Early, thick-boosted American-type loader, with mixed flowers.
The fruits are short, dark green, granular with an average weight of 70-90g. After processing
it remains harder, crisper than smooth varieties.Pickled cucumber
Early type, mixed flower, high yield variety. The fruits are short,
they are ribbed, their weight is 70-90 g, their color is dark green with black spines.

name: Cucumber Goblin (gerkin)
description:
Early to flower and set fruit. High powdery mildew tolerance
Up to 50 crunchy and juicy fruits per plant Semi-trailing plants (spread 40cm) ideal for patio containers
Plants are bred to be semi-trailing and are ideal for larger patio containers. Fruits can be harvested in about 8 weeks from transplanting. Pick regularly when fruits are 5cm 'cornichons' or when they are 10cm long for pickling or salad use.
plantingOutInstruction:
GROWING ON: Gradually acclimatise plants to outdoor conditions before
planting out after last frosts. Leave 75cm (2.5ft) between plants in each direction. Do not remove the male flowers. Best grown outdoors, allow to trail on the ground or plant in larger patio containers.
sowingInstructions: SOWING INSTRUCTIONS: Sow seed 13mm (1/2in) deep in 7.5cm (3in) pots of good seed compost. Place pots in a propagator or seal in a polythene bag and keep at 21-25°C (70-77°F) until after germination which usually takes 5-7 days. Alternatively, sow seed directly into the soil outside once it has warmed and there is no further risk of frost. Sow at a depth of 2cm (3/4in) 75cm (2.5ft) apart and in rows 75cm (2.5ft) apart.
careInstructions: Ensure no 'all female' varieties are also being grown so as to avoid cross pollination. Feed with potash fertiliser once fruiting commences.

name: Cucumber Marketer
description:
Cucumis sativus
A popular variety producing heavy yields of smooth, dark green fruits. Perfect for salads.
plantingOutInstruction: lant out in desired location when all chance of frost has passed. Harden off first.
sowingInstructions:
Indoor Planting:
Sow seeds 0.5cm deep in pots of moist compost, be careful not to over-water. Store in a warm location at an approx. temperature of 20°c (68°f). P
careInstructions:
Pick fruit regularly and feed well. Keep well watered in dry conditions.
Keep free from weeds.

description:

Succulent and superb-tasting peas
• On average 9-11 peas per pod
This well-known, heavy-cropping heritage pea variety is one of the most popular tall varieties - plants can grow to 1.8m (6ft), so support is essential. row and attach pea netting or chicken wire. The pods will be ready to harvest about 12-13
weeks from sowing. Pick regularly for higher yields and to extend the picking season.

name: Pea Ambassador

Allow 60cm between each row. Seedlings will usually appear after 14-21 days.
careInstructions: When the seedlings emerge insert plant supports, wire or netting for support. Pick pods regularly to maximise cropping. Keep the soil moist and weed free.

name: Pea Mangetout Shiraz

Powdery mildew resistant and tolerance to downy mildew to help extend the sowing season to early July.

careInstructions: GROWING INSTRUCTIONS: Water plants regularly, especially when in flower as this will improve the crop. Start picking pods just as the peas inside start to form, regular picking will encourage further cropping and improve the flavour.

name: Potato Colleen (first early)
description: Solanum tuberosum
plantingOutInstruction: Planting-out can take place as soon as the risk of frost has passed in your area (March-May). Dig over and cultivate the ground to be planted, removing any weeds. Raise shallow ridges 60cm/24" apart and plant the seed potatoes into the ridge12cm/5" deep and 22cm/9" apart. If the potatoes have been chitted, take care not to damage the chits (shoots) as you plant. When the plants reach approx. 20cm/8" tall, draw earth up the sides of the plant (covering the lower leaves). name: Tomato 'Giant Delicious' mari mari
description:
Solanum lycopersicum 'Delicious' ('Red Delicious')

• Huge Beefsteak fruits are filled with juicy meaty flesh.
• One slice will fill a sandwich.
• Suitable for protected and outdoor growing.

sowingInstructions:
Tomato seed is easy to germinate and grow on provided you practise good hygiene, use the freshest possible seed compost, and keep a careful eye on temperature, watering and light. Sow the seed thinly onto gently firmed trays or pots of compost – about ten seeds to a 3½" (9 cm) pot, or a couple of hundred seeds to a standard seed tray (you can divide up the tray to sow a number of varieties if you wish). Cover the seed with a layer of vermiculite or sieved fresh seed compost roughly as thick as the seeds themselves.
Water the trays or pots and stand them somewhere warm and in good light. A constant temperature of 64-77°F (18-25°C) is perfect, so if you have a heated propagator that is ideal; alternatively, a warm windowsill will be fine. Avoid putting the tray or pot in a plastic bag as this can create excessive humidity and the possibility of fungal problems. Keep the compost just moist but never soggy. At a temperature of 75°F (24°C) seeds should germinate within five to ten days; a cooler temperature will slow down germination, and below 50°F (10°C) the seeds will probably not germinate at all.
Once the seeds have germinated, keep a very close eye on them as the seedlings can turn leggy very quickly. Provide as much light as you possibly can and grow the seedlings on at a reduced temperature of around 65°F (18°C). If you are growing them on a windowsill or using a similar uni-directional light source you will need to turn the growing container several times a day to ensure that the seedlings do not grow towards the light. Watering is also important – too much water and you will produce weak, leggy seedlings. It is better to let the compost all but dry out before watering again rather than keeping the compost at a 'steady moist'. Once the seedlings have produced their first true leaves (that is, the first set of leaves after the seedling leaves) prick out (transplant) your seedlings into modules or small pots. As with all seedlings, hold them by their leaves rather than their stems when pricking out. If the seedlings are a little leggy you can set them deeper to shorten the height of the seedling, as tomato seedlings will stem-root.
careInstructions:
• This is an indeterminate variety and best grown as a cordon (vine).
• Support of the developing crop with strings, canes or similar will be essential!
• For best yields stop at 3rd or 4th truss if growing under protection (2nd or 3rd outside).

pruningInstructions: Remove all side shoots as they appear. Pinch the growing tip when the plant has formed seven trusses under cover or four trusses outdoors. Tie the main stems to their supports and remove any sideshoots that develop between the main stem and the leaf stems. Once the plant has produced 6 or 7 trusses, pinch out the top of the main stem. This process of "sideshooting" and "stopping" will increase the availability of light and air movement around the developing fruit, and focus the plants energy on producing a good crop of high quality tomatoes.
